title: Evaluating Tuning Opportunities of the LLVM/OpenMP Runtime
problem: Tuning parallel applications on multi-core architectures is difficult and existing auto-tuning approaches only utilize standard OpenMP features (thread count, placement, binding, scheduling) while ignoring the additional configuration parameters provided by OpenMP implementations like LLVM/OpenMP.
motivation: Comprehensive characterization of LLVM/OpenMP runtime tuning opportunities is essential for optimizing HPC and datacenter applications across diverse CPU architectures.
method: Exhaustive exploration of LLVM/OpenMP runtime configuration options collecting 240,000 samples across three CPU architectures using benchmarks (NAS Parallel Benchmarks, Barcelona OpenMP Task Suite, XSBench, RSBench, SU3Bench, LULESH). Linear Models machine learning algorithms analyze relationships between architecture, application, input size, thread count, and environment variables to identify performance patterns and generate recommendations.
key_novelty: Systematic exhaustive characterization of LLVM/OpenMP runtime tuning opportunities through ML-based analysis to derive architecture-aware configuration recommendations and optimal defaults.
contributions: Exhaustive exploration of LLVM/OpenMP runtime configuration parameters across three CPU architectures
Identification of architecture-aware tuning trends and recommendations
Architecture-specific default configurations derived from empirical analysis
Open-sourced dataset of 240,000 tuning samples for community use

metrics.other: tuning potential per architecture and application

limitations: Specific performance metrics and quantitative improvements not detailed in abstract.
